decisions.executionNote: Begin left-arm approach to basket handle, gradually turning fingers downward; board specifies a red/white-labelled bottle. Keep right arm clear.
Retry rejected basket approach with smaller increments to preserve elbow-up joint continuity.
Track the moving basket with the left arm, raising link6 for a downward handle grasp; watch continuity during faster forward approach.
Reduce rotation and translation after IK rejection, continuing left approach without changing elbow branch.
Smaller continuous approach steps after rejected targets; left gripper remains open above the moving basket.
Basket is traveling into the right workspace; switch to right-arm interception rather than crossing the left arm. Keep left stationary and clear.
Advance right gripper above basket path with continuous downward rotation; target bottle has not yet arrived in the visible central belt.
Position right wrist over the moving basket handle and rotate the open gripper toward a top grasp; retain separation from the left arm.
Replan from executed prefix: align across the basket's right rim and close gently while tracking its belt motion. Rim contact is not yet a confirmed grasp.
Test basket retention by raising the closed right gripper vertically; verify basket follows before completing the required lift.
Basket did not rise with the first test. Reopen and lower toward its right rim while matching conveyor motion for a deeper sidewall grasp.
Close around the contacted right basket rim, pause to settle, then make a small retention-test lift. Prior descent was impeded by contact.
Re-seat the open right fingers slightly lower over the moving rim, then close while matching belt travel; basket retention is still uncertain.
Raise the closed right grip by 10 cm to test and complete the basket lift; judge retention by basket motion rather than command tracking.
Basket now rotates with the right grip; add lift clearance while keeping it closed. Prepare the left gripper above the incoming-object lane without crossing arms.
Hold the raised basket and move the left open gripper above the incoming lane, completing its downward orientation. Await the board-matching bottle.
Basket slipped during suspension. Reopen and align a more vertical grip over its right sidewall; leave the left arm at its last accepted configuration.
Insert the more vertical right fingertips below the basket rim and close fully, allowing the unsettled basket to seat before another lift.
Lift the newly seated rim grip 10 cm with the right gripper commanded fully closed; monitor the basket rather than aperture telemetry.
Keep the retained basket closed, bring it nearer and slightly toward the shared center, and gently level its opening while adding lift margin.
Hold the visibly suspended basket steady. Lower the open left gripper toward the incoming-object lane while preserving reach margin; wait for the pictured bottle rather than pick distractors.
Replan after continuity rejection: retract slightly and tilt the left fingers forward for a reachable side approach to incoming objects. Keep basket suspended in the right grip.
Continue a shallow forward-facing left grasp approach above the conveyor; basket remains stable and raised. The purple container and white tools do not match the board.
Pause at the observed safe approach pose while the conveyor advances; retain the raised basket and visually search for the red/white bottle.
Shift the left arm slightly nearer and lower to clear sight of a red/white item entering behind it; maintain a shallow grasp approach and a stationary closed basket grip.
Move the left open gripper nearer the foreground bottle lane, clear of the white distractor, and lower gradually toward a side grasp. Keep the lifted basket fixed.
Left descent encountered interference. Withdraw upward and outward to clear distractors and reveal the arriving bottle; maintain the basket's closed elevated grip.
The matching white/red bottle with dark cap is now visible lying ahead of the left arm. Approach its body from the near side, allowing for conveyor travel; keep basket raised.
The wrist view confirms the red/white target bottle between the approaching fingers. Close while tracking its travel, then lift slightly to check retention; keep basket raised.
Bottle remained on the belt and moved toward the foreground. Reopen and correct the left grasp toward its visible body, nearer and slightly left of the prior pinch.
Bottle body is now visible between the left fingers. Close fully with slight conveyor tracking, settle, and lift 3 cm to check retention while right basket remains raised.
The bottle was not retained. Re-seat farther toward the foreground so its body reaches the fingertip pinch region, track its rightward travel, then close again.
Bottle body is seated between the left fingers. Keep fully closed and lift clear of the belt while beginning a slow inward transfer; retain the elevated basket.
The shallow tail grip slipped during the lift. Reopen, lower, and shift right toward the bottle's middle with a slightly steeper grasp angle; basket remains suspended.
Close on the bottle's central label now aligned between the fingertips, seat slightly deeper, and test retention with a vertical 4 cm lift.
The side pinch missed again. Change to a steeper top grasp with the open left hand above the bottle, tracking its rightward motion; keep the basket held steady.
Align the steeper left grasp with the middle of the moving bottle, descend another 3 cm, and close fully around its body.
Test the deeper central-body grasp with a slow vertical lift, holding both grippers fully closed and checking whether the bottle follows.
Bottle is still below the fingertips. Reopen and descend more deeply with the steeper grasp, placing pads around the body instead of pinching above it.

Correct rightward alignment: bottle has drifted outside the left pinch. Move the raised basket farther into the right workspace to clear access, and center the left jaws on the bottle without crossing midline.
Keep the newly centered bottle grip closed and lift vertically without lateral acceleration, checking retention before transfer toward the raised basket.
Bottle remains ahead and right of the pinch. Make a deeper, forward correction while keeping the left wrist on its own side, and close near the bottle body beside the basket.
Withdraw the closed left grasp upward and slightly left to verify retention and avoid pushing farther into the right workspace; keep the basket closed and steady.
Bottle has moved into the right workspace. Bring the held basket toward the center and align the open left hand with its left rim, preparing a supported handover without crossing arms.
Continue bringing the basket's left rim into the left jaws and close for dual support. Keep the right hold until left retention is established.
Left jaws contacted the outside wall rather than seating. Clear the rim upward with an open hand, ease the held basket underneath, and reduce right-arm extension slightly while maintaining elevation.
Lower and center the still-held basket enough to clear the left fingertips, then seat the left jaws over its rim for supported transfer; avoid further extension.
Disengage the obstructed left approach completely: retract and raise the open hand above the rim before centering it. Keep the right basket hold fixed.
Center the left pinch farther inward over the accessible basket rim while lowering from clearance; close for shared support, leaving the right grip engaged.
Test the left basket support by releasing the right hand and withdrawing it gently within the right workspace. Left remains fully closed; inspect whether the basket stays suspended.
Left now supports the basket; begin gently leveling it while moving it left. Approach the visible target bottle with the free right hand from above, staying in its own workspace.
Basket slipped from the left hand. First secure the nearby target with a deeper right top grasp while it remains reachable; clear the left hand for subsequent basket recovery.
Test right bottle retention with a vertical lift. Lower the open left hand toward the basket's newly settled left rim for recovery, keeping the wrists on their respective sides.
Right bottle pinch was left of its body and too high. Correct rightward and downward before closing; simultaneously seat the left basket-rim grip while following belt motion.
Test both newly seated grasps by lifting with closed jaws, drawing the basket gently left while raising the right bottle grip vertically.
Basket follows the left grip; add lift margin. The right pinch is still above and behind the traveling bottle, so reopen and make a larger downward/rightward correction within the right workspace.
Target is ahead and right in the wrist view. Advance the right open pinch onto its body at belt height, then close while tracking; keep the basket stably lifted in the left hand.
Bottle remains forward-right of the right pinch. Use a shallower approach to extend the fingertips without fully extending the arm, then close around the visible body; left basket stays elevated.
Use wrist orientation to reach forward-right toward the bottle's near end rather than stretching the elbow farther. Reopen and close only after the correction; maintain the raised basket.
Catch up to the traveling bottle with a faster but bounded rightward approach, aiming the fingertips toward its near end. Keep the lifted basket stationary and monitor reach continuity.
Replan after reach-continuity rejection: do not extend farther. Retract slightly and use wrist rotation to aim the fingertips toward the bottle's near end, then close; basket remains held.
Use the remaining reach margin for a small forward/downward correction onto the bottle's near end, closing only after seating. Keep the basket suspended and avoid a large joint jump.
Do not continue the rejected extension. Close at the observed bottle contact, then retract and lift gently to test retention while restoring right-arm reach margin.
The bottle was not retained. Reorient the right fingertips more directly toward the outer belt without further arm extension, opening for a final reachable near-end approach; maintain basket hold.
With the wrist redirected and reach margin restored, make a small forward approach toward the bottle's nearest end and close; keep the basket held motionless.
Make a final small near-end correction with a nearly horizontal right approach; do not compensate beyond any rejected prefix. Keep the left basket grip closed and elevated.

The target is beyond the safe near-end grasp and was not retained. Retract the right arm to restore elbow-up reach margin rather than stretch farther; keep the basket securely elevated and monitor the belt.
Retry the rejected withdrawal from the unchanged observed pose using smaller increments; preserve the held basket and restore right-arm reach margin.
Continue the safe right-arm withdrawal and turn back toward the reachable conveyor area. The bottle is not held; preserve the lifted basket while monitoring for another reachable opportunity.
Return the empty right gripper to a compact, reachable waiting pose. Keep the basket lifted in the left hand and watch the conveyor; the target has traveled beyond safe reach.
Continue returning the empty right arm to a safe elbow-up waiting pose, clear of the held basket. Monitor for any reachable target opportunity without claiming placement.
Finish resetting the free right wrist to a compact downward-ready posture. Maintain the left basket hold and watch the belt for a reachable target.
Maintain the suspended basket and safe right-arm waiting pose while monitoring the conveyor. The target is not in the basket and no reachable object is currently visible.
Hold the basket elevated with the left gripper closed and keep the right arm clear. Continue visual monitoring; no reachable target is visible and placement is not complete.
Maintain the elevated basket and clear right-arm waiting posture while monitoring the conveyor. Target placement remains incomplete; no reachable target is visible.
Keep the basket suspended with the left grip closed and the right arm safely clear. Continue monitoring for a reachable target; placement is not complete.
